card.name: Small words before durations and intervals
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as for, every and a that come right before a length of time or dosing interval, e.g. 'dose for the shortest duration', 'every 6 hours', 'for a few weeks'.

modes.label: for before duration
modes.description: The word 'for' after 'lowest effective dose' or 'treatment', leading into how long something lasts.
modes.example: use the lowest effective dose<< for>> the shortest duration possible.

modes.label: every before interval
modes.description: The word 'every' after a dose, leading into hours between doses.

modes.label: a before time span
modes.description: The word 'a' after 'for', leading into a time span or patient description.
modes.example: which may last for<< a>> few weeks.

card.writes: It seems to suppress 'while'-type words, steering the text toward a time span or interval instead.
card.plain: It fires on the small word just before a length of time or dosing interval, like 'for' or 'every' ahead of '6 hours'.
